meta.name: USS Missouri (BB-63)
meta.summary: Iowa-class fast battleship as modernized in 1984–86 and now a museum ship at Pearl Harbor. 887 ft 3 in (270.4 m) long, 108 ft 2 in (33 m) beam. Eight Babcock & Wilcox boilers (600 psi, 850 °F) in four fire rooms alternating with four engine rooms; four General Electric geared turbine sets, 212,000 shp on four shafts. Eight 1,250 kW ship's service turbogenerators and two 250 kW emergency diesels. This profile covers the engineering plant; weapons are modeled for layout only. Fault guidance is general Navy steam-plant practice — the ship's EOSS and NSTM govern.

components.name: Hull, armor belt and main deck
components.desc: Hull 887 ft 3 in (270.4 m) overall, 860 ft (262.1 m) at the waterline, beam 108 ft 2 in (33 m), draft about 37 ft 9 in (11.5 m) at full load. Waterline belt 12.1 in tapering to 1.62 in below. Machinery spaces sit between turrets II and III. Drawn see-through; Hide guards removes it.
components.src: USS Missouri Memorial Association — Ship characteristics; Wikipedia — USS Missouri (BB-63)

components.name: Superstructure, funnels and masts
components.desc: Forward superstructure with the armored conning tower (17.3 in sides) and bridge, two funnels carrying the boiler uptakes, aft superstructure and foremast. The 1984–86 refit removed the mainmast and added SPS-49 and SPS-67 radars.
components.src: Wikipedia — USS Missouri (BB-63); USS Missouri Memorial Association — Ship characteristics

components.name: Turret I (16-inch, forward)
components.desc: Three 16-inch/50 Mark 7 guns. Turret face armor 17 in (19.5 in with backing), sides 9.25 in, top 7.25 in. Rotating structure on a roller path inside the barbette, trained and elevated by electric-hydraulic drives. Shown for layout only.
components.src: USS Missouri Memorial Association — Ship characteristics; Wikipedia — USS Missouri (BB-63)

components.name: Turret II (16-inch, superfiring)
components.desc: Superfiring turret forward of the conning tower; same construction as turret I. Shown for layout only.
components.src: USS Missouri Memorial Association — Ship characteristics

components.name: Turret III (16-inch, aft)
components.desc: Aft turret, facing astern. The after group of machinery spaces ends just forward of its barbette. Shown for layout only.
components.src: USS Missouri Memorial Association — Ship characteristics

components.name: 5-inch/38 twin mounts (six)
components.desc: Six twin 5-inch/38 dual-purpose mounts remained after the 1984–86 refit removed four. Shown for layout only.
components.src: Wikipedia — USS Missouri (BB-63)

components.name: Tomahawk/Harpoon launchers and CIWS
components.desc: Armored box launchers for up to 32 Tomahawk, quad canisters for 16 Harpoon, and four Phalanx CIWS — all added in the 1984–86 refit. Shown for layout only.
components.src: Wikipedia — USS Missouri (BB-63); USS Missouri Memorial Association — Ship characteristics

components.name: Main boilers (8 × Babcock & Wilcox M-type)
components.desc: Two boilers in each of four fire rooms (FR1–FR4), 600 psi and 850 °F superheated steam. Each has a saturated side and a superheat side with their own burners; water level is held by hand at the gauge glasses. Any boiler can feed any engine within its group (forward FR1–2/ER1–2, aft FR3–4/ER3–4). A cold boiler takes about an hour to steam.
components.src: USS Missouri Memorial Association — Ship characteristics; Naval Gazing — Iowa engineering (Engineering Part 4, engine room and auxiliary machinery photo tours)

parts.name: Water gauge glasses and remote level indicator

components.name: Forced draft blowers
components.desc: Steam-turbine-driven blowers pressurize each fire room's boiler casings with combustion air drawn through intakes in the funnels. Airflow is trimmed at the air registers to match burners in use.
components.src: Naval Gazing — Iowa engineering (Engineering Part 4, engine room and auxiliary machinery photo tours); general US Navy steam-plant practice (M-type boilers, geared turbines) — the ship's EOSS and NSTM govern

components.name: Main engines (4 × GE geared turbine sets)
components.desc: One set per engine room: HP turbine (1 impulse + 11 reaction rows, 4,905 rpm, up to 24,400 hp) and LP turbine (6 reaction rows, 3,913 rpm, 28,600 hp) with astern blading in the LP casing (11,000 hp), crossover pipe, double-reduction gear (24.284:1 HP, 19.369:1 LP), main condenser under the LP turbine and main thrust bearing. About 53,000 shp at 202 shaft rpm per set; designed for 20% overload. ME1 is in ER1, ME4 in ER2, ME2 in ER3, ME3 in ER4.
components.src: Naval Gazing — Iowa engineering (Engineering Part 4, engine room and auxiliary machinery photo tours); USS Missouri Memorial Association — Ship characteristics

components.name: Shafts and propellers (4)
components.desc: Four shafts: lengths 340, 243, 179 and 277 ft from starboard to port. Inboard shafts carry five-bladed 17 ft 5 in propellers, outboard shafts four-bladed 18 ft 3 in propellers. Line shaft bearings, strut bearings and stern tube seals along each run.
components.src: Naval Gazing — Iowa engineering (Engineering Part 4, engine room and auxiliary machinery photo tours); USS Missouri Memorial Association — Ship characteristics

components.name: Steering gear and twin rudders
components.desc: Two rudders, each moved by its own electro-hydraulic steering gear (rams and motor-driven variable-delivery pumps) in the after steering rooms. Steering is normally from the pilot house, with local (trick wheel) control aft as backup.
components.src: USS Missouri Memorial Association — Ship characteristics; general US Navy steam-plant practice (M-type boilers, geared turbines) — the ship's EOSS and NSTM govern

components.name: Feed system (DFTs and feed pumps)
components.desc: Condensate from each main condenser goes to the deaerating feed tank (DFT) in the fire room, held just below boiling to strip oxygen, then booster and main feed pumps deliver it to the boiler economizers. Main feed pressure is held above drum pressure.
components.src: Naval Gazing — Iowa engineering (Engineering Part 4, engine room and auxiliary machinery photo tours); general US Navy steam-plant practice (M-type boilers, geared turbines) — the ship's EOSS and NSTM govern

components.name: Fuel oil service system
components.desc: About 2.5 million gallons of fuel in double-bottom and wing tanks. Converted from heated Navy Special Fuel Oil to distillate (DFM) in the 1980s, so tank heating was removed. Service pumps and duplex strainers in each fire room feed the burners; atomizing is by steam.
components.src: USS Missouri Memorial Association — Ship characteristics; Naval Gazing — Iowa engineering (Engineering Part 4, engine room and auxiliary machinery photo tours)

components.name: Main lube oil system
components.desc: Each engine room has its own sump under the reduction gear, attached and motor-driven lube oil pumps, strainers, coolers and a purifier. It feeds the turbine and gear bearings, gear sprays and the main thrust bearing.
components.src: general US Navy steam-plant practice (M-type boilers, geared turbines) — the ship's EOSS and NSTM govern

components.name: Main circulating water and air ejectors
components.desc: Sea water through the main condensers comes in by scoop injection at speed and by the main circulating pumps at low speed or astern. Air ejectors draw off non-condensable gas to hold vacuum, roughly 12–14 psi below atmospheric (colder sea water gives more vacuum).
components.src: Naval Gazing — Iowa engineering (Engineering Part 4, engine room and auxiliary machinery photo tours)

components.name: Ship's service turbogenerators (8 × 1,250 kW)
components.desc: Two steam turbogenerators in each engine room, each 1,250 kW, 480 V, 3-phase, 60 Hz (about 2,005 A), with its own condenser and zinc anodes. Combined capacity about 10 MW.
components.src: Naval Gazing — Iowa engineering (Engineering Part 4, engine room and auxiliary machinery photo tours)

components.name: Main and emergency switchboards
components.desc: Four main switchboards (one per engine room) in three sections — upper, lower and a control benchboard with metering, generator breaker controls and governor controls — plus two emergency switchboards in the auxiliary machinery rooms. Shore power comes in on 400 A cables.
components.src: Naval Gazing — Iowa engineering (Engineering Part 4, engine room and auxiliary machinery photo tours)

components.name: Emergency diesel generators (2 × 250 kW)
components.desc: Two diesel generators in the forward and after auxiliary machinery rooms, each 250 kW AC with a 5.5 kW DC output, feeding the emergency switchboards when ship's service power is lost. Started with compressed air from receivers.
components.src: Naval Gazing — Iowa engineering (Engineering Part 4, engine room and auxiliary machinery photo tours); general US Navy steam-plant practice (M-type boilers, geared turbines) — the ship's EOSS and NSTM govern

components.name: Distilling plants (evaporators)
components.desc: Steam-heated distilling plants make boiler feed makeup and fresh water from sea water. About 239,000 gallons of fresh water are carried. Salinity cells on the distillate dump bad water to the bilge or reserve tanks.
components.src: USS Missouri Memorial Association — Ship characteristics; general US Navy steam-plant practice (M-type boilers, geared turbines) — the ship's EOSS and NSTM govern

components.name: Anchor windlass and ground tackle
components.desc: Bower anchors with chain led through hawse pipes to the windlass on the forecastle.
components.src: general US Navy steam-plant practice (M-type boilers, geared turbines) — the ship's EOSS and NSTM govern

faults.title: Low water in a boiler
faults.msg: Water out of sight in the gauge glass (low)
causes: Feed check or feed regulator valve closed or stuck
Main feed pump lost or low discharge pressure
Gauge glass valves shut or glass blocked — false reading
Large steam demand change (shrink and swell)
Tube rupture
checks: Treat water out of sight low as a casualty: secure fires in that boiler immediately
Do not add feed to a boiler whose water level cannot be seen — cold water on hot tubes can rupture them
Check the second gauge glass and the remote level indicator against each other
After it cools, inspect tubes and drums before relighting
faults.src: Naval Gazing — Iowa engineering (Engineering Part 4, engine room and auxiliary machinery photo tours); general US Navy steam-plant practice (M-type boilers, geared turbines) — the ship's EOSS and NSTM govern
faults.safety: Superheated steam at 600 psi and 850 °F is invisible and lethal. A steam leak in a main space means evacuating or fighting it per the casualty procedure; never look for a leak by feel.

faults.title: High water / carryover to the turbines
faults.msg: Water high in the gauge glass; turbines knocking
causes: Overfeeding by hand
Feed regulator stuck open
Contaminated boiler water foaming (high chemistry)
Sudden drop in steam demand
checks: Reduce feed and blow down surface to bring level back in sight
If water reaches the turbines (knocking, vibration), slow or stop the engine and open the turbine drains
Check boiler water chemistry and blow down as directed
faults.src: Naval Gazing — Iowa engineering (Engineering Part 4, engine room and auxiliary machinery photo tours); general US Navy steam-plant practice (M-type boilers, geared turbines) — the ship's EOSS and NSTM govern
faults.safety: Superheated steam at 600 psi and 850 °F is invisible and lethal. A steam leak in a main space means evacuating or fighting it per the casualty procedure; never look for a leak by feel.

faults.title: Boiler tube leak or rupture
faults.msg: Rising makeup demand, steam in the firebox, falling level
causes: Overheating from low water or scale
Fireside corrosion or erosion from soot blowing
Oxygen pitting from poor deaeration
checks: A ruptured tube means securing fires and the boiler per the casualty procedure
Check DFT performance and feedwater oxygen
Track makeup water use: a slow rise points to a small leak
faults.src: general US Navy steam-plant practice (M-type boilers, geared turbines) — the ship's EOSS and NSTM govern
faults.safety: Superheated steam at 600 psi and 850 °F is invisible and lethal. A steam leak in a main space means evacuating or fighting it per the casualty procedure; never look for a leak by feel.

faults.title: Smoke from the funnel (black or white)
faults.msg: Black smoke or white smoke at the stack
causes: Black: too little air for the burners in use (registers closed, blower slow)
Black: dirty or wrong-size atomizer sprayer plates
White: far too much air, or water in the fuel
checks: Check the smoke periscope and set air registers to the burners lit
Change to clean atomizers sized for the load
Check fuel for water at the strainers and tank sounding
faults.src: Naval Gazing — Iowa engineering (Engineering Part 4, engine room and auxiliary machinery photo tours); general US Navy steam-plant practice (M-type boilers, geared turbines) — the ship's EOSS and NSTM govern

faults.title: Loss of fires or flareback
faults.msg: Burners out; or flame blows back out of the burner opening
causes: Water in the fuel or fuel suction lost
Fuel pressure drop (clogged strainer, pump failure)
Forced draft lost while burners are lit
Relighting without purging the furnace
checks: Shut the burner valves, then purge the furnace with air before relighting
Shift to the clean side of the duplex strainer and check fuel pressure
Never relight off hot brickwork
faults.src: general US Navy steam-plant practice (M-type boilers, geared turbines) — the ship's EOSS and NSTM govern
faults.safety: Flareback can burn anyone at the burner front. Purge the furnace before any relight.

faults.title: Forced draft blower failure
faults.msg: Blower stops or air pressure falls
causes: Turbine governor or steam supply fault
Bearing or lube oil failure on the blower
checks: Cut burners to match the remaining air; secure the boiler if air cannot be restored
Check blower lube oil level and bearing temperatures
faults.src: general US Navy steam-plant practice (M-type boilers, geared turbines) — the ship's EOSS and NSTM govern

faults.title: Loss of main condenser vacuum
faults.msg: Vacuum falling on the throttle board gauge
causes: Main circulating pump lost or scoop flow blocked (slow speed, fouling)
Air ejector failure or low steam to the ejectors
Air leak at gland seals or condenser joints
Condensate level too high, flooding tubes
checks: Slow the engine to the vacuum available
Start the circulating pump if the ship is slow or backing; check the scoop and sea chest
Check gland seal steam and air ejector steam pressure
Check condensate pump suction and hotwell level
faults.src: Naval Gazing — Iowa engineering (Engineering Part 4, engine room and auxiliary machinery photo tours); general US Navy steam-plant practice (M-type boilers, geared turbines) — the ship's EOSS and NSTM govern

faults.title: Low lube oil pressure to a main engine
faults.msg: Lube oil pressure alarm at the throttle board
causes: Pump failure or suction lost
Clogged strainer
Low sump level or leak
Water in the oil (cooler leak) reducing pressure
checks: Start the standby pump; shift strainers
If pressure cannot be restored, stop the engine and engage turning gear when it is safe
Check sump level, sample for water and run the purifier
faults.src: general US Navy steam-plant practice (M-type boilers, geared turbines) — the ship's EOSS and NSTM govern
faults.safety: Do not open the reduction gear or turbine casings at sea. Locked gear hatches exist to keep objects out.

faults.title: Hot bearing (turbine, gear, thrust or line shaft)
causes: Low oil flow to that bearing
Water or dirt in the oil
Shaft misalignment or a damaged line shaft or strut bearing
checks: Slow the shaft and increase oil flow if possible
Check oil temperature out of the cooler and the cooler sea water
Sample oil; inspect strainers for babbitt flakes
faults.src: general US Navy steam-plant practice (M-type boilers, geared turbines) — the ship's EOSS and NSTM govern

faults.title: Turbine vibration after stopping or on warm-up
faults.msg: Vibration or rubbing as the turbine is brought up
causes: Turbine left stationary while hot — the rotor sags (bows)
Turning gear not run after steam was shut off
Water in the casing
checks: Keep turning gear on after securing until the rotor is cool
Warm up slowly on turning gear before admitting steam
Open casing drains before warming
faults.src: Naval Gazing — Iowa engineering (Engineering Part 4, engine room and auxiliary machinery photo tours); general US Navy steam-plant practice (M-type boilers, geared turbines) — the ship's EOSS and NSTM govern
faults.safety: Do not open the reduction gear or turbine casings at sea. Locked gear hatches exist to keep objects out.

faults.title: Shaft won't answer the bell / both throttles
faults.msg: Shaft rpm does not match the order
causes: Ahead and astern throttles open at the same time
Throttle valve stuck or linkage fault
Steam pressure low for the speed ordered
checks: Never have ahead (green) and astern (red) open together
Check main steam pressure to the engine room
Full ahead to full astern takes time — reverse in steps
faults.src: Naval Gazing — Iowa engineering (Engineering Part 4, engine room and auxiliary machinery photo tours)

faults.title: Main feed pump failure / low feed pressure
faults.msg: Feed pressure falls toward drum pressure
causes: Pump turbine governor fault
Feed booster pump lost — main feed pump flashing
DFT level low
checks: Start the standby feed pump at once and watch boiler levels
Check booster pump discharge and DFT level
If feed cannot be restored, secure the affected boilers
faults.src: general US Navy steam-plant practice (M-type boilers, geared turbines) — the ship's EOSS and NSTM govern

faults.title: DFT level high or low
causes: Low: makeup not keeping up, condensate pump problem
High: too much makeup or excess drains — deaeration stops working
checks: Adjust makeup feed and recirculation to restore level
High oxygen in feed follows a flooded DFT: check samples
faults.src: general US Navy steam-plant practice (M-type boilers, geared turbines) — the ship's EOSS and NSTM govern

faults.title: High salinity in condensate or feed
causes: Condenser tube leak letting sea water into the condensate
Distilling plant making bad water
Contaminated reserve feed tank
checks: Find the source by checking each salinity cell in turn
Isolate the leaking condenser half if possible; plug the tube in port
Dump bad distillate; do not send it to the boilers
faults.src: general US Navy steam-plant practice (M-type boilers, geared turbines) — the ship's EOSS and NSTM govern

faults.title: Water or sediment in fuel oil
faults.msg: Burners sputter; water at the strainers
causes: Tank not stripped after ballasting or refueling
Condensation in partly empty tanks
checks: Shift suction to another tank
Strip water from the service tank
Clean strainers and watch for loss of fires
faults.src: general US Navy steam-plant practice (M-type boilers, geared turbines) — the ship's EOSS and NSTM govern

faults.title: Ship's service generator trip / loss of power
faults.msg: Generator breaker open; lights out on part of the ship
causes: Overload after another generator dropped off
Reverse power while paralleled (governor fault)
Low steam pressure to the turbine
Overspeed trip
checks: Shed non-vital loads and restart or parallel another generator
Emergency diesels pick up the emergency switchboards
Check governor settings and load sharing at the benchboard before reclosing
faults.src: Naval Gazing — Iowa engineering (Engineering Part 4, engine room and auxiliary machinery photo tours); general US Navy steam-plant practice (M-type boilers, geared turbines) — the ship's EOSS and NSTM govern
faults.safety: 480 V switchboards carry enough fault current to kill. Only qualified electricians work inside them, with the bus de-energized and tagged out.

faults.title: Emergency diesel won't start
faults.msg: EDG cranks slowly or not at all
causes: Low starting air pressure in the receivers
Fuel shut or day tank low
Control power or start relay fault
checks: Check air receiver pressure and the start air valves
Check the fuel day tank and fuel rack
Test the EDG weekly so this is found in port
faults.src: general US Navy steam-plant practice (M-type boilers, geared turbines) — the ship's EOSS and NSTM govern

faults.title: Steering casualty
causes: Steering pump motor lost (power)
Hydraulic leak or low oil in the rams
Control (follow-up) failure from the pilot house
checks: Shift to the standby pump and the other power supply
Take local control in the steering room (trick wheel)
Use the shafts to steer if both rudders are lost
faults.src: general US Navy steam-plant practice (M-type boilers, geared turbines) — the ship's EOSS and NSTM govern

faults.title: Fuel oil fire in a main space
faults.msg: Fire in a fire room or engine room
causes: Fuel spray from a leaking flange or gasket onto hot surfaces
Oil-soaked lagging
checks: Follow the main space fire doctrine: secure fuel at the remote cut-outs, evacuate and fight from outside
Do not re-enter until the space is cleared
faults.src: general US Navy steam-plant practice (M-type boilers, geared turbines) — the ship's EOSS and NSTM govern
faults.safety: Main space fires kill quickly. The ship's casualty procedure governs.

io.desc: Steam drum water level — two gauge glasses plus remote indicator, per boiler
Fuel oil pressure to the burner manifold
Forced draft air pressure in the boiler casing
Main feed pump discharge pressure (held above drum pressure)
Makeup feed flow / reserve feed tank level
Main condenser vacuum (about 12–14 psi below atmospheric)
Lube oil temperature out of the cooler
Bearing temperatures (turbine, gear, thrust, line shaft)
Shaft revolutions (202 rpm at full power)
Generator load per SSTG (1,250 kW rating)

sequence.name: Light off a boiler
sequence.desc: Line up feed and fuel, start the forced draft blower and purge the furnace, light one burner, then raise pressure slowly with drains open. A cold boiler takes about an hour.

sequence.name: Warm up the main engine
sequence.desc: Turning gear on, gland seal steam on, start circulating and condensate pumps, raise vacuum with the air ejectors, then admit warming steam with drains open.

sequence.name: Test throttles and steering
sequence.desc: Disengage turning gear, spin the shaft ahead and astern on the throttles, test steering in all modes and check rudder angle indicators.

sequence.name: Underway
sequence.desc: Answer bells at the throttle board; light more boilers for higher speed (four boilers normally, all eight for full power, two for economy).

sequence.name: Electrical plant
sequence.desc: SSTGs paralleled on the main switchboards with load shared; emergency diesels in standby on the emergency switchboards.

sequence.name: Secure the plant
sequence.desc: Stop the engine, close throttles, keep turning gear on while the turbine cools, secure fires and let boilers cool slowly.

checks.name: Watch rounds — fire rooms
checks.why: Water level and fuel are where boiler casualties start.
steps: Compare both gauge glasses and the remote level indicator
Blow down gauge glasses as scheduled
Burner fronts: no leaks, atomizers clean, smoke periscope clear
Fuel strainer differential and fuel pressure
DFT level and feed pressure margin above drum pressure
checks.src: general US Navy steam-plant practice (M-type boilers, geared turbines) — the ship's EOSS and NSTM govern

checks.name: Watch rounds — engine rooms
checks.why: Lube oil and vacuum problems give warning before damage.
steps: Lube oil pressure and temperatures; sump level
Bearing temperatures along the turbine, gear and thrust bearing
Shaft alley: line shaft bearing temperatures and oil levels
checks.src: general US Navy steam-plant practice (M-type boilers, geared turbines) — the ship's EOSS and NSTM govern

checks.name: Boiler water and feed chemistry
checks.why: Scale, oxygen and salt cause tube failures.
steps: Test boiler water and feed as scheduled
Never send salty distillate to the feed system
checks.src: general US Navy steam-plant practice (M-type boilers, geared turbines) — the ship's EOSS and NSTM govern

checks.name: Electrical plant checks
checks.why: Loss of power takes out steering, pumps and lighting.
steps: Emergency diesels started and loaded on schedule
checks.src: general US Navy steam-plant practice (M-type boilers, geared turbines) — the ship's EOSS and NSTM govern

checks.name: Steering test before getting underway
checks.why: A steering casualty in a channel is the worst time to find it.
steps: Test each pump and each power supply
Test local control from the steering room
checks.src: general US Navy steam-plant practice (M-type boilers, geared turbines) — the ship's EOSS and NSTM govern

Voltage, frequency, kW and current metering
Speed/load control for paralleling and load sharing
Normal and alternate supply to the steering gear

defects.name: Boiler tube failure
defects.looks: Blistered, bulged or split tubes; scale inside; pits on the water side.
isolate: Section a failed tube and look inside: scale means overheating, pits mean oxygen

defects.name: Propeller cavitation erosion
defects.looks: Frosted, pitted patches near blade tips and the back of the blades; noise at high speed.
isolate: Inspect in dry dock; map pitting against blade radius

defects.name: Condenser tube erosion and leaks
defects.looks: Thinned inlet ends, pinholes, rising condensate salinity.
isolate: Leak-test each condenser half in port

causes.cause: Sea water velocity and entrained sand at the inlet
causes.fix: Inlet inserts; keep sea chests clear

defects.name: Hull fouling
defects.looks: Growth on the hull; more rpm needed for the same speed; higher fuel use.
isolate: Compare rpm per knot with the clean-hull figure

causes.cause: Long periods at anchor in warm water
